newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ireland's TSB Bank says raises interest rates.
newsitem.headline: Ireland's TSB Bank says raises interest rates.

text.p: Ireland's TSB Bank said on Thursday it was raising most of its interest rates by between 25 and 50 basis points.
TSB said it was "the final major bank to raise its rates in the current round of rate increases".
The variable home loans rate was increased by 25 basis points to 7.0 percent while the two-year fixed home loans rate was raised by 30 basis points to 7.25 percent.
The five-year fixed home-loans rate was lowered, however, by 25 basis points to 8.50 percent.
"In relation to future trends, we do not accept that further increases are inevitable in the near future," Chief Executive Harry Lorton said in a statement.
A number of Irish banks and building societies have raised their interest rates in recent weeks, following a tightening of wholesale rates in the Irish money market.
